film.title: Bowling Green, Ohio: The Lightest Banner in Basketball
film.description:
Every school we cover gets a video on its best player before March. Bowling Green goes first, with a Hall of Famer: Nate Thurmond. Two MAC titles, a win over No. 2 Loyola in February 1963, and 31 rebounds against Mississippi State the night after the Game of Change, still the Bowling Green record. Then the pros: Wilt's backup, seven All-Star games, the first official quadruple-double. Then he came home to Cleveland, and the Cavaliers retired #42 after 114 games. So we did the math on every retired number in the NBA. Pound for pound, it is the lightest banner in basketball. We love him anyway.

Narrated by Matthew Hagan, who appears as an AI video avatar made with HeyGen. Charts by Hardwood Bricks; data as of November 17, 2026.

Local history... and college basketball. See more at https://hardwoodbricks.com

reels.title: The Lightest Banner: thirty-one rebounds
reels.text: March 16, 1963. The night after the Game of Change, Nate Thurmond grabbed 31 rebounds against Mississippi State. It is still the Bowling Green record. A minute from our new film, The Lightest Banner in Basketball.

reels.title: The Lightest Banner: Cleveland's number 42
reels.text: We love Nate Thurmond. We also have a spreadsheet. 114 games and 566 points for Cleveland, and the Cavs retired his number first. Pound for pound, the lightest banner in basketball. From our new film.
